audit.description: Changed production files replace matplotlib/seaborn plotting imports with real Plotly usage via `from plotly import graph_objects as go`, and construct `go.Figure`, `go.Scatter`, and `go.Bar` objects in plotting functions. Static and dynamic evidence show no production `matplotlib` imports or source-library runtime attempts, while dynamic target events resolve Plotly from site-packages and report no local target provider.
evidence: ash_model/viz/static.py: removed `import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`; added `from plotly import graph_objects as go` and uses `go.Figure`, `go.Scatter`, and `go.Bar`.
ash_model/viz/temporal.py: removed `matplotlib.pyplot` and `seaborn`; added `from plotly import graph_objects as go` and uses Plotly figures/traces.
anti_cheat_static file_checks: `ash_model/viz/static.py` and `ash_model/viz/temporal.py` have `imports_target: true`, `imports_source: false`, `fake_target_added_code: false`.
anti_cheat_dynamic metrics: `source_imports_from_production_repo_count: 0`, `target_events_from_production_repo_count: 8`, `target_local_spec_count: 0`, Plotly origin under site-packages.
reasons: Production plotting code meaningfully uses Plotly graph_objects APIs.
Static checks report no source imports or dynamic source use in changed production files.
Dynamic evidence observed Plotly imports and attribute access from production code.
No local fake Plotly provider or target sys.modules alias was detected.
